summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout/AAPS data show 86.0% time in range, mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, and 5.1% time below range with recurrent early-night and post-afternoon lows. Coverage is good. The selected profile is complete and declared applicable. No carbs were logged, so UAM and SMB are the observed meal engine. Afternoon highs then evening crashes are not isolated to the 16:00 basal of 0.5 U/h. Competing leftover-IOB, target-90, DynISF, and overnight-basal explanations are not separated, so every inventory item is kept.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM is usable for later inference: 3995 valid entries, 98.7% coverage, 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, no invalid or duplicate points. The authoritative aaps_profile is complete for basal, CR, ISF, targets, DIA, and the six AAPS groups. Hourly local glucose is complete. Carb telemetry is empty rather than incomplete CGM.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality status good; included_counts show 15 daily rows and 24 local hourly rows; treatment_summary carb_entries 0 and total_carbs_g 0; carb_treatment_entries empty; profile_context historical_applicability yes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carb entries; only sampled treatments and loop statuses; Aug 7 and Aug 21 incomplete; u200 dilute label unquantified; mid-period profile switch, GLP-1 notes, and a 19 Aug occlusion are unquantified confounders.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety is the binding constraint. TBR is 5.1% with extremes to 41-42 mg/dL and highs to 290-293 mg/dL. CV is 32.6%. Local TBR clusters at 23:00-03:00, especially hour 1 at 18.5%, and at 18:00-19:00, especially hour 19 at 15.3%. Several correction windows show large two-hour falls after modest insulin, consistent with stacked IOB rather than an isolated basal hole.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary; hourly_glucose_local; daily_glucose worst TBR on 11 Aug 9.4% and 18 Aug 12.8%; glucose_extremes; therapy_response_windows including 234 to 56 mg/dL and 264 to 96 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality coverage is adequate for hypo review even without carbs.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No hypo-treatment or activity logs; IOB available only in sampled loop rows; cannot yet split basal versus leftover automation insulin.

analysis_steps.findings: Late-night to morning recovery after 04:00 and 05:00-08:00 TIR of 97-98% do not show a high-basal dawn picture. Early-night TBR sits on target 90 mg/dL and basal 0.6 U/h. Afternoon TAR peaks at hour 16 while 16:00 basal is already the lowest segment at 0.5 U/h. Evening TBR follows that peak, so raising 18:00-19:00 basal is not supported. Day target 100 mg/dL is not the afternoon-high driver.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local means and TBR/TAR by hour; basal_segments 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.7/0.5/0.6/0.7 U/h; target_segments 90 then 100 then 90 mg/dL; temporary targets of 135 mg/dL on several days.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR forbids basal increases; automation not yet separated from basal.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting-night experiment; COB always 0; 13 Aug profile switch; GLP-1 and temporary-target use confound overnight reads.

analysis_steps.findings: CR segments exist but were unused: 0 g logged and sampled loop rows show cob 0. Flat profile ISF 56 mg/dL/U is stronger than a rough 1500-1800/TDD estimate from about 20 U/day, but DynISF is on and sampled variable_sens ranges about 28-124. DIA 10 h is conservative and is compatible with late evening and overnight lows; nothing isolates DIA as too long or too short.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_ratio_segments 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, 12.6 g/U; isf_segments 56 mg/dL/U; dia_hours 10; representative_loop_statuses variable_sens; therapy_response_windows mixed rises and steep falls.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets overnight lows must not be blamed on ISF alone; automation_sensitivity_limits needed before any ISF move.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal composition, no ISF test, DynISF dominates delivered sensitivity, insulin-concentration label unresolved.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM always-on with 3-minute interval, 15-minute SMB and 20-minute UAM basal minutes is internally consistent with a no-carb workflow. High temporary targets can pause SMB. Sampled delivery exceeds a naive profile-basal times 15-20 minutes, including SMB 0.3-0.4 U and a 1.6 U UAM high-boost row, with enacted temps near 4 U/h. This stack can explain late peaks then 18:00-19:00 TBR better than a weak afternoon basal.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_settings smb_enabled true, uam_enabled true, smb_always_enabled true, cob and after-carb SMB false; representative_loop_statuses reasons; representative_treatments temp basals to 0 and above 3 U/h.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Only 24 loop snapshots; plugin boost phrasing not fully specified; no meal timestamps to prove UAM versus unlogged food.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is false; a sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not proof of Autosens. DynISF at 70% compresses ISF at peaks. max_iob 25 U and max_basal 12 U/h do not bind versus TDB 16.2 U/day and observed IOB about 4.7-5.9 U; temps clip near 4 U/h. Carb-absorption settings are idle while COB is 0 and are not duplicate UAM counting.
analysis_steps.evidence: raw_settings autosens_enabled false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent 70, max_iob_units 25, max_basal_u_per_hour 12, min_5m_carbimpact 8, meal_max_absorption_hours 7; loop insulinReq and variable_sens rows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: DynISF formula version not in package; 19 Aug occlusion coincides with high IOB; no controlled ISF or fasting test.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared analysis_context has meal_strategies empty and strategy_stable_for_period null. No prebolus_minutes or immediate_bolus_percent exists to reproduce. Observed execution is correction boluses plus SMB/UAM, not wizard meals. The meal problem is insulin after the rise plus leftover IOB, not a calculable immediate percent.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.analysis_context meal_strategies []; carb_entries 0; 24 therapy_response_windows all Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false; local rise from about 09:00 and hour-16 TAR 32.1%.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets; profile_cr_isf_dia unused CR; automation_smb_uam; automation_sensitivity_limits.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Declared meal-strategy fields are null or empty; Nightscout has no carb timestamps or bolus-before-rise flags.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, start offset, or duration is declared. Telemetry has zero extended-carb entries. E-carbs are not a pump extended bolus. Inventing graze e-carbs for hour-16 TAR is unsupported and would stack on already-active UAM. Morning and afternoon rises look like one unannounced-UAM pattern, not two meal programs.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries 0; carb_treatment_entries []; idle min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours; GLP-1 notes on 14, 17, and 20 Aug as unquantified confounders only.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked e-carb or absorption observations; meal composition is not in the package and was not inferred.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked 18:00-19:00 TBR: first DynISF plus frequent UAM SMB, second leftover IOB with DIA 10 h and evening basal 0.6-0.7 U/h, third site, occlusion, or GLP-1 outliers. Ranked 23:00-03:00 TBR: first target 90 mg/dL plus residual evening IOB, second 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h, third new overnight SMB. Afternoon TAR is not a 16:00 basal defect. CR and e-carbs cannot be the primary fix while carbs stay at 0. Package data override any earlier impulse to change ISF, SMB, DynISF, or caps together. Conservative plan: keep the whole inventory, verify overnight lows against IOB, then log meals, then consider one automation lever only if those observations separate the cause.
analysis_steps.evidence: Checkpoints 1-3 reconciled to aaps_profile, profile_context applicability yes, decision_inventory 23 complete current values, hourly_glucose_local, empty meal declaration versus UAM-only telemetry.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Still no fasting-night IOB log and no yes/no carb log for usual eating times.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7% with good quality status and complete local hourly rows.
Overall TIR 86.0% with strong 05:00-08:00 stability and recovery after 04:00.
Selected profile is complete and declared historically applicable; labeled 16-2u basal matches calculated TDB about 16.2 U/day.
SMB activation flags match a no-carb UAM workflow, and high temporary targets can pause SMB.
Autosens target shifts are off, so overnight target is not being auto-lowered.
issues: Time below range 5.1% with recurrent 41-54 mg/dL lows clustered at local 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00.
Afternoon TAR peaking at hour 16 then crashing, consistent with late UAM/DynISF insulin rather than a single profile hole.
Glucose variability CV 32.6% and several severe highs to about 290 mg/dL.
Zero logged carbs while CR is time-varying, so meal CR cannot be tested.
DynISF 70% with profile ISF 56 mg/dL/U compresses sensitivity at peaks; max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h do not bind.
Mid-period profile switch, site and sensor changes, GLP-1 notes, and a 19 Aug occlusion/pump error remain confounders.

recommendations.title: Keep the basal and target profile and separate leftover IOB from overnight basal
recommendations.description: Early-night TBR overlaps target 90 mg/dL and basal 0.6 U/h, but afternoon UAM/DynISF already creates leftover IOB into the evening. Morning fasting-like hours are stable and 16:00 basal is already the lowest segment, so no profile insulin increase is supported. The first review action is observation, not a value change.

suggested_change.review_direction: Keep all basal and target segments. Next review 00:00 basal only if 23:00-03:00 lows persist on nights with near-zero late IOB.

recommendations.title: Keep SMB, UAM, and DynISF until meals are logged
recommendations.description: Changing SMB interval, UAM minutes, DynISF, and profile ISF together would not be separable. Meal-strategy fields are empty and carbs are 0, so automation is the current meal engine and should stay unchanged until a short carb yes/no log exists.

suggested_change.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_change.review_direction: Do not change SMB/UAM or DynISF in the same step as basal, ISF, or CR. Revisit one automation lever only after overnight IOB and meal logs exist.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current basal schedule, including 0.6 U/h at 00:00, and verify early-night lows against leftover evening IOB before any profile edit.
profile_recommendation.rationale: 05:00-08:00 is the strongest fasting-like window. Hour-16 TAR occurs while basal is already 0.5 U/h. Overnight TBR can be residual UAM/DynISF IOB plus target 90 mg/dL rather than excess 00:00 basal. Package evidence does not separate those causes, so a basal change is unsupported.
profile_recommendation.next_check: On several nights, record local IOB and whether SMB/UAM ran after 21:00; if 23:00-03:00 TBR continues when IOB is already near zero, review 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h as the single next profile item.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 23-03 show TBR 10-18.5% with hour-1 mean 90.6 mg/dL. Uncertainty: leftover evening IOB and target 90 mg/dL are competing causes. Dependencies: do not change this with target, DIA, SMB, or DynISF. Change unsupported until low-IOB nights are observed.

Evidence: hour 5 mean 104.2 mg/dL, TIR 95.2%, TBR 4.8%. Uncertainty: one 42 mg/dL extreme is later at hour 7 after a sensor change. Dependencies: morning stability also depends on overnight leftover IOB. No isolated 05:00 defect.

Evidence: hours 6-8 means about 99-110 mg/dL and TIR 98% class. Uncertainty: 21 Aug 06:19 low of 42 mg/dL follows a sensor change. Dependencies: safety_overview forbids using one extreme to raise or cut this segment.

Evidence: hours 9-12 rise with TAR up to 20% is compatible with unannounced intake and UAM, not a unique 10:00 basal hole. Uncertainty: no carb timestamps. Dependencies: CR unused; SMB/UAM is the meal engine. Do not raise daytime basal.

Evidence: hour 16 mean 162.8 mg/dL and TAR 32.1% occur on the already-lowest basal. Uncertainty: UAM delay versus food versus GLP-1. Dependencies: raising 16:00 basal would stack on DynISF/SMB into the 18:00-19:00 TBR cluster.

Evidence: hour 18 TBR 7.7% after the afternoon peak. Uncertainty: residual SMB/UAM versus this basal. Dependencies: safety_overview and meal stacking. An increase is unsafe; a cut is not separated from automation.

Evidence: hour 19 TBR 15.3% is the evening crash window. Uncertainty: 0.7 U/h may add to leftover IOB but is not shown as the primary cause. Dependencies: do not change with SMB delivery or DynISF in the same step.
Evidence: 0 g carbs logged and cob 0 in sampled loop rows, so this CR was unused. Uncertainty: unknown whether overnight snacks occur. Dependencies: meal logging must exist before any CR review.
Evidence: no carb treatments in this or any segment. Uncertainty: unused setting cannot be validated. Dependencies: UAM-only execution; changing CR would not alter current delivery.
Evidence: morning rise is UAM/corrections without announced carbs. Uncertainty: breakfast composition unknown. Dependencies: do not pair a CR change with SMB or ISF.

Evidence: this is the most aggressive CR but it was unused while hour-16 TAR was highest. Uncertainty: if logging starts, this window would need fresh data. Dependencies: afternoon TBR risk; unused CR is not the current lever.
Evidence: no evening carb entries; evening issue is TBR after earlier insulin. Uncertainty: dinner logging absent. Dependencies: leftover IOB and DIA 10 h dominate this window.

Evidence: flat 56 mg/dL/U with DynISF on and variable_sens about 28-124; correction windows both overshoot and fail. Uncertainty: profile ISF cannot be isolated from DynISF 70%. Dependencies: do not change ISF and DynISF together; overnight TBR also depends on target and IOB.

Evidence: overnight target 90 sits inside the 23:00-03:00 TBR cluster. Uncertainty: residual IOB may be the true driver. Dependencies: tightening this target is unsafe; raising it is a later single-lever option only after low-IOB nights are reviewed, not a supported change now.

Evidence: daytime target 100 mg/dL is not aligned with hour-16 TAR 32%. Uncertainty: temporary targets of 135 mg/dL also appear. Dependencies: afternoon highs are UAM/meal-timing issues, not this target.
Evidence: 23:00 returns to 90 mg/dL as TBR rises. Uncertainty: same leftover-IOB confound as 00:00 target. Dependencies: keep with 00:00 target; do not move overnight targets and basal together.

Evidence: late crashes after afternoon insulin are compatible with long action or same-day stacking. Uncertainty: no rows show IOB already near zero with unexplained late lows, or the reverse. Dependencies: DIA, ISF, and SMB must not change together.

Evidence: switches match zero-carb telemetry and cob 0. Uncertainty: cannot tell UAM-only-by-design from unlogged meals. Dependencies: meal log first; disabling UAM now would remove the only observed meal delivery without a declared bolus plan. No source component is null so verify is not used.

Evidence: always-on SMB is what arms delivery; COB flags are idle; high TT SMB-off matches TT 135 events. Uncertainty: always-on plus UAM may over-deliver after unannounced rises. Dependencies: do not change activation with interval or DynISF in one step.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 3-minute UAM stacking and sampled SMB 0.3-1.6 U can explain 18:00-19:00 TBR. Uncertainty: DynISF may be the larger amplifier. Dependencies: withhold a frequency change until overnight IOB and meal logs separate causes. Remaining wait text is not this interval.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: observed IOB about 4.7-5.9 U and temps near 4 U/h never approach 25 U or 12 U/h, so caps are non-binding rather than the hypo cause. Uncertainty: lowering caps would be a safety-backstop idea, not a proven fix, and would mix with SMB strength. Dependencies: do not change limits with SMB or DynISF together.

Evidence: Autosens is independently false; sensitivity_ratio near 1 is neutral. DynISF 70% with ISF 56 mg/dL/U compresses peak ISF. Uncertainty: cannot quantify how much of the crash is DynISF versus UAM frequency. Dependencies: do not change DynISF and profile ISF together. Keep Autosens off until a profile lever is chosen.

Evidence: settings are idle with cob 0 and are not UAM double-counting. Uncertainty: they would matter only after carb logging starts. Dependencies: meal_ecarbs_absorption; do not invent e-carb durations from these defaults.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the observed UAM-first pattern: no guessed prebolus minutes, no guessed immediate-bolus percent, and no e-carb template. Leave SMB/UAM as the only meal delivery until clock time, carbs yes/no or grams, and any pre-rise bolus are logged.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared analysis_context meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so there is no declared prebolus or percent to reproduce. Telemetry shows 0 g carbs, no e-carbs, and correction-plus-UAM execution. Afternoon highs then 18:00-19:00 lows fit late UAM plus leftover IOB, not a missing e-carb graze.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For 3-5 usual eating occasions, record clock time, carbs yes/no with grams if known, and whether any bolus was given before the rise.

exceptions.pattern: Late-day peak then evening crash, local about 14:00-19:00
exceptions.suggestion: Do not add e-carbs, an assumed immediate percent, or stronger UAM in this window.
exceptions.rationale: This is the highest TAR then the highest post-peak TBR; extra meal insulin would not be separable from DynISF, 3-minute UAM, DIA 10 h, and evening basal.

implementation_steps: Treat this as decision-support review only: independently check every value against the pump and AAPS screens before considering any edit.
Keep the full selected profile and all six AAPS inventory groups unchanged in this pass.
First observation: on several nights note local IOB and late SMB/UAM after 21:00 and whether 23:00-03:00 lows still occur when IOB is already near zero.
Second observation: log 3-5 usual eating times with carbs yes/no or grams and any pre-rise bolus so UAM-only-by-design can be separated from unlogged meals.
If those observations later support one edit, change only one dependent area at a time: overnight basal or overnight target, not both, and not with ISF, DIA, SMB, or DynISF.
Do not introduce a guessed prebolus, immediate-bolus percent, or e-carb schedule while carb fields remain empty.
Re-review after one small verified change or after the two observation logs, using the same local-hour TBR and afternoon TAR windows.
education: UAM is not the same as counted COB; sampled loop rows stayed at cob 0, so CR and e-carb settings did not drive this fortnight.
A sensitivity_ratio near 1 is a neutral current adjustment and does not mean Autosens is enabled; Autosens is separately off.
Dynamic ISF can make delivered sensitivity much stronger than the flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U at high glucose.
A late peak followed by an evening low can be stacked insulin from SMB/UAM rather than afternoon basal that is too low.
E-carbs are an absorption announcement, not a pump extended bolus, and should not be inferred from an average without meal-linked entries.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice. TuneMyBG prepares data for review only.
Independently verify every proposed change, make at most one insulin-delivery change at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Time below range is 5.1% with documented lows to 41-42 mg/dL; do not tighten the overnight 90 mg/dL target or strengthen ISF, SMB, or UAM while that cluster is unexplained.
Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h did not constrain observed delivery; they are not a current safety backstop.
Discuss any future setting review with the care team, especially around overnight hypoglycemia, pump occlusion events, and GLP-1 notes.
